Prymorsk Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zaporizhia Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Prymorsk — known as Nohaisk until 1964 — once had a cemetery divided into four sections: Christian, German, Armenian, and Jewish. Only the Christian section survives today; a local resident, Totya Masha, recalls the Jewish section being demolished in the 1960s or 1970s, and a local architect involved in its demolition was reportedly taken to court over it, though he has since died. About 200 Jews from the town and surrounding areas were murdered by German forces in November 1941, out of a community that had once numbered over 500.
